questions.prompt: Which of these changes to an existing endpoint calls for a new API version?
options: Adding a new optional field to the response
Adding a brand new endpoint
Renaming a field in the response
Adding an extra log line to the action
questions.explanation: Removing or renaming a field, changing a type, status codes or auth requirements are breaking changes. Additive changes such as a new optional field or endpoint usually stay in the current version.

source.section: Step 1: Understand why you version APIs

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson say URL path versioning (`/api/v1/orders`) is the most common choice for internal and enterprise .NET APIs?
options: It is explicit and simple to reason about, and easy to route
It is the most RESTfully pure option
It keeps URLs clean by moving the version to a header
It is the only scheme `Asp.Versioning.Mvc` supports
questions.explanation: URL path versioning is explicit, cache-friendly and easy to route; its downside is that it "pollutes" the URL. The media type scheme is the most RESTful, and the setup can combine URL, header and query readers.

questions.prompt: You want clients to move off v1 without breaking them yet. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Delete `OrdersV1Controller` and let old clients get 404
Mark it `[ApiVersion(1.0, Deprecated = true)]` so the response headers tell clients to migrate
Point the v1 route at the v2 controller
Set `AssumeDefaultVersionWhenUnspecified = false`
questions.explanation: Deprecating instead of deleting keeps v1 working while the `api-supported-versions` / `api-deprecated-versions` headers signal the change. The policy is to support N-1 and sunset older versions on a schedule.

questions.prompt: You register one Swagger document per version but don't add a `DocInclusionPredicate`. What do you see?
options: Only the v1 document is generated
Swagger UI fails to load
Deprecated versions are hidden
Every version's document lists all controllers, V1 and V2 mixed together
questions.explanation: By default Swashbuckle puts every action into every document. `DocInclusionPredicate` decides, per operation, whether it belongs in the document being built.

questions.prompt: A health-check action has no `[ApiVersion]` attribute. Where does the lesson's `DocInclusionPredicate` put it?
options: In every Swagger document
In no Swagger document
Only in the v1 document
Only in the newest version's document
questions.explanation: When an action has no version metadata the predicate returns `true`, a safety fallback that includes it everywhere rather than hiding it.

questions.prompt: What does the `SwaggerDefaultValues` operation filter do?
options: Decides which Swagger document each operation appears in
Fills in default values for request parameters
Sets OpenAPI's `deprecated` flag on operations whose API version is marked deprecated
Adds the version dropdown to Swagger UI
questions.explanation: `operation.Deprecated |= apiDescription.IsDeprecated()` marks each operation of a deprecated version, so Swagger UI shows it struck through. Choosing the document is the predicate's separate job.
